Assessed pass/fail on technical proficiency, artistic expression and reflective capacity.

So the door is open on the strength of demonstrated practice, not credentials — but he currently has no portfolio, which is exactly the 'relevant experience' the sentence turns on.
liveAudition: NO — no audition and no interview is mentioned anywhere on the programme page. Admission is on the application plus the portfolio. This is the cleanest gate in the block.
portfolioSpec: Exact: 'A portfolio that provides selected examples of your recent original creative work, (audio, video or other formats as appropriate, four to six separate pieces). These should be provided as links to streamable content (on English Language sites). Examples should be relevant to the focus of the pathway'. So: four to six separate pieces, recent, original, delivered as streaming links (SoundCloud/Vimeo/YouTube — not files), matched to the pathway he names. No total duration is prescribed.
tunisianCost: GBP 22,000 per year — 'International - full-time: £22000' for 2026/2027 entry. Roughly EUR 25,000/yr, before London living costs and before the visa and IHS surcharge.
funding: Thin and not aimed at him. The page names a 'Global Ethnic Majority Music Scholar's Fee Waiver', 'a full-tuition fee-waiver scholarship [that] aims to support a GEM student who intends to progress through postgraduate study and into an academic research position', and the 'Sarah Caple Award' for 'Funding to enable students to further their studies or musical development'. deadline: Rolling: 'We accept applications from October for students wanting to start the following September.' No fixed closing date; 'Late applications will only be considered if there are spaces available.' For September 2027 that means applying from October 2026 onwards, and early, since funding and places go first.
language: English. IELTS requirement: '6.5 with a 6.5 in writing and no element lower than 6.0'. He has not sat IELTS, and the 6.5-in-writing sub-score is the specific thing to train for.
verdictWhy: Academically this is the best-fitting door on the list — an explicit route in for a non-music degree with relevant experience, a clean four-to-six-piece portfolio, no audition, and a popular-music-production pathway aimed at exactly what he wants to become. It fails on money alone: GBP 22,000 a year plus London living, with no funding he has been shown to be eligible for. Build the four-to-six-piece portfolio anyway — it is the reusable asset that unlocks İTÜ MİAM, Ghent and UNATC — but do not spend the Goldsmiths application unless a full fee waiver materialises.
